column47: Description

The accounting major provides the tools for students to understand the accounting information that is used by managers within firms (for decision-making), by capital market participants (for valuation), and by corporate stakeholders (for monitoring and contracting). The major provides a strong foundation that prepares students for a variety of career paths, including investment banking, investment management, management consulting, and corporate finance. Students intending to pursue a career in public accounting should consider the CPA track which helps students to meet the requirements of the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) exam.

column47: The primary objective of the doctoral program in accounting is to train students for careers in research and teaching at the university level. Accordingly, the program provides rigorous training in the theoretical foundations and empirical tools of accounting, finance and economics. Students work closely with faculty in seminars and research projects. The relatively small size of the program provides an opportunity for students to have extensive interaction with faculty. Students begin to do active research early in the program. Students develop expertise in the major fields in accounting: financial accounting and managerial accounting. Students also develop expertise in a minor field such as economics, finance, or statistics. Faculty in the Accounting Department have a wide range of research interests including the role of accounting information in capital markets, corporate governance, performance measurement, managerial incentives, and taxation. The department sponsors two research workshop series and a series of occasional conferences that bring leading researchers to campus.

column47: The PhD program in Applied Economics at the Wharton School is a full-time, residential program for students interested in applying economic analysis to a wide range of real-world issues. The program provides students with a rigorous training in economic theory and econometrics and helps them develop into first-rate researchers. Students in the program take courses from and engage in research with faculty from across the Wharton School and the University of Pennsylvania. The faculty are members of a number of departments including: Accounting; Business Economics and Public Policy; Finance; Health Care Management; Management; Marketing; and Real Estate. Wharton’s Applied Economics PhD program offers students a unique opportunity to focus on a particular area of applied economics while having strong connections to the broader Wharton community. Students in Wharton's Applied Economics PhD program typically focus on a specific area of applied economics that aligns with one of the fields of study at Wharton. Examples include: Accounting; Behavioral Economics; Business Economics and Public Policy; Ethics and Legal Studies; Finance; Health Economics; Management; Marketing; Operations, Information, and Decisions; and Real Estate. Students receive a degree in Applied Economics, and their dissertation must be on a topic in applied economics. The program trains students for careers in academic research, government and industry. All students admitted to the Wharton PhD Program are awarded a fellowship that covers the full cost of tuition and fees, health insurance, and a generous living stipend.

column47: The major in Artificial Intelligence for Business will combine a thorough grounding in the fundamentals of AI with a deep dive into how AI is being used in practice across a wide range of industries, including finance, marketing, healthcare, retail, and transportation. Students will be prepared to step into key roles in the AI-powered economy, whether that is starting a new venture that uses AI, joining an established firm to help them build out their AI capabilities, or investing in the next generation of AI-based companies. The major will draw on faculty and courses from across the University to offer unparalleled breadth and depth at the intersection of AI and business.

column47: The undergraduate concentration and MBA major in Asset Management/Impact Investing (previously called the Capital Markets and Portfolio Management specializations at the undergraduate level and the Investment Management major at the MBA level) prepares students for careers in asset management, including security analysis, portfolio management, sales and trading, and impact investing. Asset management involves investing on behalf of individuals and institutions. Asset management is a large and growing industry which offers many exciting career opportunities. The growth is fueled by the rising demand for retirement products around the globe as well as by the creation of new investment products, such as exchange-traded funds, and new investment strategies, such as hedge funds and private equity. The Asset Management/Impact Investing program provides a deep understanding of the investment process and the institutional features of financial markets. The program integrates theory and practice, and provides students with the analytical tools to analyze a wide variety of investment opportunities and to create investment portfolios that are tailored to the specific needs of different investors. The curriculum provides a strong foundation for all students interested in the area of investments. Beyond the core courses, the curriculum allows students to specialize in security analysis and valuation, portfolio management, impact investing, or quantitative finance. Our students obtain jobs in security analysis, portfolio management, hedge funds, sales and trading, financial advising, and impact investing.

The Business Analytics major provides students with state-of-the-art training in data analytics and its applications in business. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the role of data analysis in business, hands-on experience with modern data analysis tools, and a clear vision of how data analysis can be used to improve business decisions. The major builds on the foundation laid in the core curriculum and prepares students for careers that require the ability to use data and analysis in a variety of business functions. The course of study is structured to have students work with a wide variety of data to address real business problems.

Students will learn how to:

- Build and interpret predictive models using a wide variety of data sets, including those with a very large number of variables (Big Data);
- Construct and analyze optimization models for business applications such as logistics, pricing, and scheduling;
- Apply data analysis techniques such as conjoint analysis and social media analytics to develop better understanding of consumer behavior; and
- Use data analytics to analyze risk and make investment decisions.

Overall, the major is designed to provide students with the kind of hands-on experience and deep understanding of data analytics that is in great demand in a wide range of industries. It provides an excellent foundation for careers in a wide range of fields, including consulting, finance, marketing, and operations. The goal is not simply to provide a set of specific data analysis skills, but to provide a deeper understanding of the kinds of business problems to which they can be applied.

column47: The Business Economics and Public Policy (BEPP) major equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand the economic, political and social context in which businesses operate and to formulate effective business strategies. The modern business enterprise is confronted with a dynamic and challenging environment at home and abroad. Rapid advances in technology, changing consumer preferences, and evolving national and international government policies all have a profound impact on a business’s bottom line. At the same time, corporations are being called upon to consider how they can better serve a wide array of stakeholders, including not just shareholders but also their employees and the communities in which they operate. The BEPP major prepares students to understand these issues and formulate private and public strategies that can promote both business performance and social welfare. A major in Business Economics and Public Policy is especially suitable for students who anticipate careers in finance, management in regulated industries, management in industries that are facing new public policy challenges (such as the tech industry), management consulting, and entrepreneurship.

Students may concentrate in either ethics or legal studies. Because of the interdisciplinary nature of the field, the curriculum is flexible enough to accommodate individual student interests. column47: Finance applies economic theory to the problems of business and financial management. Finance is concerned with the acquisition and allocation of funds by a business firm, by a financial institution, or by a government agency. The efficient allocation of funds requires an analysis of the various sources of funds and a determination of the least-cost combination. Once obtained, funds are used to finance assets, which, in turn, are expected to generate income. The analysis of the proper balance between risk and return determines the value of the firm. Because the allocation of funds in an economy is carried out mainly through financial markets and intermediaries, the department also emphasizes the study of the functions and operations of these institutions. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels.

The Finance PhD program at Wharton provides students with a solid foundation in the theoretical and empirical tools of modern finance, drawing on a rigorous economic framework. Students are prepared for academic careers in research and teaching at leading institutions. The program provides students the flexibility to pursue their own research interests within the broad spectrum of topics in the field of finance. The program curriculum is enhanced by the close interaction of the Finance Department with the school’s other departments and the University’s Department of Economics. In addition, the department’s research centers, the Rodney L. White Center for Financial Research and the Wharton Financial Institutions Center, provide students with extensive resources, including data and faculty support. Students work closely with faculty, whose interests span a wide variety of topics. The faculty is consistently ranked among the most productive in the profession, and faculty research is regularly featured in top academic journals and the financial press on a regular basis.

column47: The Health Care Management (HCM) major, the first and largest of its kind, provides in-depth exposure to the theory and practice of health care management. Students gain an understanding of the complex economics of health care, its delivery, financing, and policy. Each entering class of approximately 75 students begins its study in the summer with a pre-term orientation program. Over the two-year period, students complete the Wharton core curriculum and the required health care courses. Health Care Management majors typically come from a variety of backgrounds, but many have prior experience in the field. Students benefit from the program’s close ties to the University of Pennsylvania Health System and the Leonard Davis Institute of Health Economics. Career opportunities for graduates are numerous and diverse, including positions in health care finance, hospital and health system management, pharmaceutical and biotechnology sales and marketing, health care entrepreneurship, and government.

The Wharton PhD Program in Health Care Management and Economics prepares students for careers in academia, government, and the private sector, in positions requiring a sophisticated understanding of the economics and management of health care. The program draws on a variety of basic disciplines including economics, sociology, and political science to build a set of conceptual and empirical tools for analyzing the special problems of the health care sector. The program’s faculty are national and international leaders in health economics and management research. Wharton’s health care faculty have done pioneering work in the areas of risk adjustment, the study of insurance markets, the economics of the pharmaceutical industry, and the impact of managed care and other new forms of organization on the cost and quality of care. Students also benefit from Wharton’s broad strength in management, and from University-wide resources such as the Leonard Davis Institute of Health Economics (LDI). Students completing the program will have the skills to do original, high-quality research on the management, organization, and economics of health care, and to teach in a university or professional school setting.

Our doctoral students are prepared for careers at top academic institutions and for leadership roles in business and government. They learn to conduct original research by working with faculty who are leaders in their fields.

The Marketing major provides students with the necessary skills to succeed in a wide range of careers including brand management, business development, consulting, entrepreneurship, general management, marketing research, product management, retailing, and sales. The foundation of the Marketing curriculum is an understanding of consumer behavior and the skills to conduct and analyze marketing research. Building on this foundation, students may take courses in specific areas of marketing such as retailing, new product development, business-to-business marketing, and advertising management. column47: The joint major in Marketing and Operations Management (MKOP) is designed for students who plan to pursue careers in which a close link between marketing and operations is critical. Such careers include product management and supply chain management. This major has a two-part core requirement: a marketing core course and an operations management core course. The remainder of the course work can be selected from a wide variety of advanced courses in marketing and operations management.

The Wharton Marketing PhD Program trains students to become leading researchers and scholars in the field of marketing. Our program provides a strong theoretical foundation in the disciplines of economics, psychology and statistics, combined with the development of rigorous empirical and theoretical research skills needed for an academic career in marketing. The two broad approaches to marketing are the psychological (consumer behavior) and the economic/statistical (quantitative). Students are expected to become expert in at least one of these two approaches and competent in the other. Students work closely with faculty, often collaborating on research projects beginning in their first year. For students entering with a bachelor's degree, the program is expected to take five years to complete. The first two years are primarily devoted to coursework. At the end of the second year, students take a preliminary examination. The final two to three years are spent on developing and writing a dissertation.

column47: The Multinational Management major equips students with the specialized knowledge, skills, and perspective needed to lead in a globalized business world. This major covers subjects such as global strategic management, cross-cultural management, comparative management, and the management of multinational corporations. Students will gain a deep understanding of the economic, social, political, and legal environments in different countries and regions, and how these factors influence business operations and strategy.

The Operations, Information and Decisions department is a multidisciplinary group of faculty with core interests in decision sciences and in the design and management of business processes. Our interests span both the theoretical and the practical. We apply the disciplines of optimization, statistics, and stochastic modeling to a wide range of business problems. We also use laboratory experiments, empirical analysis, and field studies to build theories of how organizations operate, and how individuals and organizations make decisions. Students may elect to focus on one of three broad areas: Business Analytics, Decision Processes, or Operations Management/Information Systems.

column47:
The Operations, Information and Decisions department at the Wharton School is an eclectic group of scholars who are united by the goal of advancing the-state-of-the-art in our fields and by our passion for research that is both rigorous and relevant. Research in our department addresses a broad range of topics that are related to three main research areas: information systems, operations management, and decision processes.

Students in the PhD program align themselves with one of these three groups:

Information Systems: Research in this area is focused on understanding the economic and social impacts of information technology. The information systems faculty have diverse training in fields such as economics, computer science, and engineering. We are united by an interest in working on important, practical problems and a desire to use a variety of methodological approaches, including econometrics, field experiments, analytical modeling, and data mining. Examples of research topics include online social networks, crowdsourcing and prediction markets, platform-based business models, online advertising, media and technology consumption, and technology and development.

Operations Management: Research in this area studies the design and management of business processes that lead to efficient and effective production and delivery of goods and services. A distinguishing feature of our group is its strength in both analytical and empirical research. Examples of research topics include supply chain management, service operations, revenue management, global operations, and health care operations.

Decision Processes: Research in this area focuses on understanding and improving judgment and decision making by managers, consumers, and other professionals, including physicians, policy makers, and intelligence analysts. This research is primarily experimental, based on laboratory studies and field experiments and it draws on a variety of theoretical traditions, including behavioral economics, cognitive psychology, and social psychology. Examples of research topics include decision making under risk and uncertainty, group and inter-temporal decision making, fairness and trust, and moral judgment.

The Social and Governance Factors for Business major provides students with a set of frameworks and tools for understanding, assessing, and solving business challenges and opportunities associated with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. The major equips students to respond to the growing demands from investors, employees, customers, and other stakeholders for business to address these issues. The major is well-suited for students preparing for a wide range of careers, including in finance (impact investing, project finance, private equity), consulting (ESG strategy, risk management), entrepreneurship (social ventures), and corporate management (sustainability, strategy, operations).

Students who wish to pursue careers focused on environmental topics are encouraged to consider the courses that will best prepare them for those roles (e.g., those on climate, energy, and supply chains). Students develop a high degree of proficiency in statistical reasoning, computational skills, and the art of data analysis, providing them the flexibility to apply their knowledge to a wide variety of application areas. The MA in Statistics and Data Science program is a STEM-designated program.

These techniques are used to analyze financial data, evaluate marketing campaigns, and predict business outcomes. Students who take this major will learn skills that will enable them to contribute to and lead teams of data scientists as well as to bring an evidence-based, data-centric culture to all aspects of an enterprise. The major also prepares students for more advanced or specialized studies at the doctoral level. While the major is a valuable standalone option for students, the major is designed to be easily accessible to students who are also pursuing another major, allowing students to combine the data analytic skills gained through the major with an application domain (e.g. accounting, finance, marketing, etc). The major is an attractive option for students interested in careers involving data analytics and business intelligence, as well as those on a finance, consulting, technology or general management track.
